pr.title: Ask Bit: quick answers, fix buttons and rules (#63, part 1)
pr.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jasondwhyte"} -->
_Requested by **Jason** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01YGtEMFvZnSp5cxW5MGErkd?thread=cmsg_01YGtEMFvZnSp5cxW5MGErkd4yrx42V2CNrsAy6nSKB54b)_

Part of #63 (stage 1: the conversation, quick answers, buttons and rules; no AI).

Before: Bit's page was a list of notes. To fix something that needed you, you went to Review loops, Repositories or Settings and used the control there. Bit couldn't answer questions. On a phone-sized screen the sidebar was hidden with nothing in its place, so only the inbox was reachable.

After: Bit's page is one conversation that the desktop window and every browser share. Four buttons ask Bit **What needs me?**, **What's running?**, **How are my loops?** and **How are my repositories?**, and it answers straight away from Orbit's own state.

When one of Orbit's own controls fixes something that needs you, Bit's note about it (and any answer that lists it) carries that control as a button: **Continue loop**, **Review again**, **Publish report**, **Sync now** or **Turn autopilot back on**.

In **Settings → Buddy → What Bit can do**, each fix has a rule:
- **Do it**: Bit does it when the item opens, says so, and skips the desktop notification.
- **Ask first**: the default. Bit offers a button.
- **Leave it to me**: Bit offers no button.

On a phone-sized screen, a menu button opens the sidebar, so every page (Bit included) is reachable.

Bit only uses Orbit's own controls. It never answers a reviewer's request to run a command or change files, never changes a repository's setup or access, and never touches reviewed code. **Publish report** is never offered for a report the credential check flagged, or for one from a pull request automatic publication wouldn't trust, and Bit checks trust again against GitHub's latest copy of the pull request just before publishing. Turning autopilot back on changes settings, so it always waits for a tap.

Before doing a fix on its own, Bit checks again that the item still needs you, Bit is still on and the rule is still Do it. If any of that has changed, it hands the item back to you or, if the item has closed, lets it go. A Do it fix that fails is tried once, then handed back.

## How

- `attention::items` gives each item the `Fix` that resolves it, or none (approvals, disputed findings, a loop that isn't converging). Publish is offered only for a current, ready report with no credential flags from a trusted source.
- `attention::announce` judges a report being published as still ready, as it does for a follow-up, so a failed publication doesn't make its item new again.
- `buddy.rs`:
  - `Rules` on `Buddy`: `do_it` / `ask_first` / `leave_it`, default `ask_first`. Keyed by the fix's own name on the wire, validated and normalized like the other buddy settings, and patchable one rule at a time.
  - Notes gain `key` (the Needs you item, so the app can offer its fix while it's open). Answers carry `question` and `lines`.
  - New note kinds `fixing`, `fixed` and `answer`, with lines in each tone.
  - `buddy::ask` writes quick answers from the snapshot.
- `Engine::flush`: an item that just opened whose rule is Do it (while Bit is on) gets a "Fixing" note instead of a Needs you note, skips the notification and joins `Engine::fixing`.
- The next tick's `do_fixes` runs a `do_fix` task for each queued fix, only while `still_mine` holds: the same open item and fix, with Bit on and the rule still Do it.
  - It is checked under the same lock as the change (`continue_loop_if`, `enqueue_if`), after the sync lock for Sync now, and before every write for publication.
  - If a fix fails, or stops being Bit's while its item is open, Bit hands it back: a Needs you note with the button, plus the notification. If the item closed, the fix is dropped.
  - Sync now counts only once the item has closed.
- `publish::By::{You, Autopilot, Bit}`: Bit's publications apply automatic publication's trust and credential holds to the fresh PR before every write, independent of the publication switch.
- New commands `use_fix {key}` and `ask_buddy {question}`, in Tauri and the browser allowlist. `use_fix` looks the item up again by key and uses the control as the app's own button does.
- App:
  - Bit's page uses Astryx chat components: notes as Bit's messages, your questions as yours, and answers as lists with buttons.
  - Notes link to **Open loop**, **Open repositories** or **Open settings**.
  - The rules are Selectors in Bit's settings.
  - `AppShell` shows its mobile menu below the md breakpoint.
  - The browser demo answers questions and runs fixes too.
- Docs: user guide (Ask Bit, Bit's buttons and rules, phone menu), README and architecture.

## Tests

- Rust:
  - `attention_tests`: the fix for each item kind.
  - `buddy_tests`: validating, patching and normalizing rules, and rule names shared with the app through a fixture. Fixing vs Needs you notes, a settings change never done on its own, and every quick answer in every tone.
  - Engine tests (`fixes_tests`):
    - Do it runs once and replaces the notification. Ask first and Leave it don't.
    - A failed fix needs you and is notified. A button runs its item's fix.
    - Turning autopilot back on, and answers in the feed.
    - Queued fixes are dropped or handed back after Stop loop, a rule change or Bit being turned off.
    - No second review is started.
    - A queued Sync now makes no GitHub requests after its rule changes while it waits.
    - A failed Do it publish is tried once across later looks.
    - Bit's publication posts nothing once the fresh PR is untrusted, trust is revoked mid-publication, or the rule changes while it waits. It does publish with auto-post off while trusted.
- App: the conversation and its links, asking a question, fix buttons and Leave it to me, rules in Settings, reaching Bit from the phone menu, demo answers and fixes, and shared option lists and default rules.
- `cargo test` (343), `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `tsc`, `eslint`, `prettier --check`, `vitest` (172) and `vite build` all pass. Checked in the demo at desktop and phone widths.

## Milo PR review

**CHANGES REQUESTED**

Repository: `analogproblems/orbit`, PR #64
Head: `9aaf81e6cedbff5f316b088377e02af8d82aab57`
Base: `6a8e0c9b60eac7b33d5fa59f30067df8642a691f`
Configuration: `self-review-v1`
Mode: cumulative static review, observed GitHub checks, isolated JUPITER head-only JavaScript tests.

### Findings requiring changes

1. **F1 · P2 — Match the rule keys across the Rust/TypeScript boundary.** `src-tauri/src/buddy.rs:93–98,139–145` uses camelCase for both `Rules` and `RulesPatch`, but `src/types.ts` and `BuddyRules` use `continue_loop`, `review_again`, and `sync_now` as object keys. Selecting any of those rules sends that snake_case key directly through `update_settings`; `deny_unknown_fields` rejects it because Rust expects `continueLoop`, `reviewAgain`, or `syncNow`. Likewise, saved engine values arrive under camelCase keys while `buddyOf` fills the snake_case keys with Ask first. Only Publish happens to agree. Align the wire names in both directions and add a shared serialization/patch test for all four rules; the current Publish-only settings tests miss this.

2. **F2 · P1 — Revalidate queued fixes before performing their side effects.** `src-tauri/src/engine/fixes.rs:35–40` drains captured items and calls `run_fix` without checking whether the item is still open or Bit/the rule still permits it. After a Do it item is queued by `flush`, turning Bit off or changing Publish to Ask first does not cancel its queued publication, including one waiting behind another publication's lock. Similarly, queueing Continue loop and then pressing Stop loop before it runs lets `continue_loop` set `stopped = false`, undoing the explicit stop. Resolve the current item and authorization at execution, and recheck after waits immediately before mutation/publication; discard stale work. Add gated tests for queued-fix → disable/rule revocation/Stop loop → execution, asserting no side effect.

3. **F3 · P1 — Preserve the live trust check for Bit's publications.** `src-tauri/src/engine/fixes.rs:74–79` sends every Publish fix through `publish(id, false, false)`. The offer checks the cached PR's trust, but `publish.rs::final_checks` applies `automatic_hold` to the freshly fetched PR only when `automatic` is true. Therefore Bit can publish without a manual tap after a formerly trusted author loses membership/collaborator status, or trust is revoked while the fix waits, provided head/base stay unchanged. The fresh fetch does not enforce the promised trusted-source restriction on this path. Add a publication origin/guard for Bit that rechecks current trust against the fresh PR before every write, while allowing its explicit Publish rule to operate independently of the ordinary auto-post switch. Test cached-trusted/fresh-untrusted and trust revocation with no GitHub write.

These are static findings; no Rust reproduction was executed. No separate suggestions.

### Scope and verification
All 25 changed files and complete patches reviewed, including attention derivation, durable feed/queue handling, rules and wire types, desktop/remote commands, UI/save feedback, demo behavior and added tests. Relevant scheduler, stop/continue, settings, publication and trust context and repository AGENTS.md were read.

Fresh checks on October 10, 2026 at 23:47 UTC show open/non-draft, unchanged pins and mergeable/clean. **CI is absent:** zero check runs, zero commit statuses and no PR-triggered workflow runs. The empty combined-status response's default pending label is not a running check. Branch metadata reports unprotected with no required-status contexts; rulesets are empty, while the branch-rules endpoint is unsupported. These observations are not proof of every applicable merge requirement.

### Executed tests and limits
JUPITER: **171 tests passed across 20 files; none failed or skipped.** Exact detached head above; base recorded as metadata, no synthetic merge.
Preparation, dependency download, offline test and bounded cleanup exited 0. Test/download OOM=false, timeout=false; 1800-second stage limits. Node24 image:
`sha256:64af3819f9275802414d7cdc38c27e9d82bd564dec4d4da87d008255d36c63b4`.

```bash

RUN=$ROOT/runs/orbit/9aaf81e6cedb-605f23af
```

Fresh private bare repository/detached worktree from the confirmed remote. Both containers verified UID1000, all capability sets zero, no-new-privileges, read-only root, 2 CPUs/4 GiB/512 PIDs, no published ports, host credentials, SSH agent or Docker socket. Only task-owned paths writable, Git metadata read-only and host results inaccessible. Dependency download alone used networking with lifecycle scripts disabled; tests used network none with no external routes. Trusted Git `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv` checks were clean before/after each stage. No source checkout changes. Services not applicable; run-scoped runtime cleanup completed, records/artifacts retained.

Rust/native/browser/build and other unconfigured tiers were **not run**. Passing JavaScript tests with mocked/demo data do not verify Rust wire contracts or engine concurrency.
Evidence: `$RUN/revision.json`, `$RUN/results/prepare.log`, `$RUN/results/npm-{download,test}.{log,isolation.json,docker-observed.json,result.json}`, `$RUN/results/cleanup.json`, and `$RUN/artifacts/`.

commit.message:
Show a menu on phone-sized screens so Bit is reachable

On narrow screens the sidebar was hidden with nothing in its place, so a
phone over Tailscale could not reach Bit or any page other than the
inbox. The app shell's own mobile drawer now takes over below the md
breakpoint.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EDJU2uY2NCz6Ch7CDHNcNA

Recheck Bit's fixes before acting, and trust on the fresh PR

- Rule names: Bit's rules are keyed by the fix's own name
  (continue_loop, review_again, sync_now) on the wire, as the app sends
  and reads them; camelCase keys were rejected or ignored. A shared
  fixture holds the default rules for both sides.
- A fix Bit does on its own runs only while it is still Bit's: the item
  is open about the same report with the same fix, Bit is on and the
  rule is still Do it. Continue loop and Review again check under the
  same lock as the change; publication checks before every write. A
  fix that stops being Bit's while its item is open is handed back with
  its button and a notification; one whose item closed is dropped.
- Bit publishes as its own origin: the trust and credential holds of
  automatic publication apply to the fresh PR before every write, for
  buttons and Do it alike, independent of the publication switch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EDJU2uY2NCz6Ch7CDHNcNA

Recheck Sync now after waiting, and try a failed Do it publish once

- Sync now, done on Bit's own, waits for a sync already running, then
  checks again that it is still Bit's before starting its own; on a
  revoked rule it starts no sync and schedules no clone updates.
  `sync_now` is folded into the fix as the lock, the check and
  `poll_holding`.
- `attention::announce` judges a report being published as still
  ready, as it already does for a follow-up. A publication that fails
  no longer makes its held or waiting item new again, so a Do it
  publish is tried once and then handed back, instead of being queued
  again on every look.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EDJU2uY2NCz6Ch7CDHNcNA

Ask Bit: quick answers, fix buttons and rules (#63, part 1)

Bit's page becomes one conversation that every window shares. Four quick
questions (what needs me, what's running, loops, repositories) are answered
by the engine from Orbit's own state, with no AI. Each Needs you item names
the Orbit control that fixes it (continue loop, review again, publish, sync
now, turn autopilot back on); Bit offers it as a button on its note and in
answers. Per-fix rules in Settings let Bit do a fix on its own, ask first,
or leave it to you. Publishing is never offered for a credential-flagged
report or an untrusted source, approvals never get a button, and changing
settings always waits for a tap.
